newsitem.title: CHILE: Banco de Chile says had merger talks with Edwards.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Chile says had merger talks with Edwards.

text.p: Banco de Chile, Chile's second largest private bank, said it has had merger talks with Banco de A. Edwards, but the discussions have since been abandoned.

"We had some preliminary discussions, but today there are no talks going on. There was no agreement to continue the talks," Banco de Chile President Adolfo Rojas told reporters at the bank's annual shareholders meeting.
Rojas' remarks confirmed rumours which had swirled in the stock market for weeks that the banks were studying a merger.
Despite the failure of the talks with Edwards, Banco de Chile has not ruled out a deal with another bank, he said.
"We'll have to see what alternatives are out there and we are not closed to anything," said Rojas.
"If (a merger) is suitable, then we'll analyze it and if it is best to grow alone, then that's what we'll continue doing."
Many Chilean banks are mulling mergers to cut costs and survive the tough competition in the industry which has squeezed profits over the last couple of years.
Analysts have said that most medium-sized banks, such as Edwards, will merge or be taken over in the near future as the battle for customers intensifies.
